transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started on the courtyard set review. We've got two options on the table — a masonry courtyard or a modular painted-timber courtyard — and we need to settle on a construction plan today so fabrication can begin. Before I make my final approval decision, I'd like to hear from each of you: structural, permits, stunt, and insurance. Please give me your reports and any concerns you have about either option. Our approved budget is $180,000, so keep that in mind as we go through this.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical structural issue. My load test yesterday found that the masonry courtyard option would exceed Soundstage 3's 600 kilograms-per-square-meter floor limit, so that option is not viable from a structural standpoint. The modular painted-timber design does pass, but only if we install a 30-millimeter load-spreading deck. My written report is still in the engineering queue, so I'm sharing this verbally now so it's on the record for today's decision.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a critical permit update. I confirmed with the local heritage-permit office this morning that the approved facade may be no wider than exactly 8 meters, and on-stage masonry cutting is prohibited. The permit clerk's email hasn't been added to the production file yet, but these are hard constraints we need to factor into today's decision.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a stunt requirement that affects the courtyard layout. My rehearsal assessment found that the scripted horse dismount requires an unobstructed lane exactly 10 meters long and 4 meters wide, with a 2-meter crash mat at its landing end. The choreography note is still awaiting the next stunt meeting, but this is a hard requirement that the chosen set design must accommodate — whichever option we go with needs to allow for that clear lane and crash mat space.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have an insurance concern to flag. I confirmed with our insurer's underwriter that coverage on Soundstage 3 excludes any open-flame brazier on this stage. However, an LED-flame prop is permitted under the policy, but only if it remains at least 12 meters from the sprinkler-head cluster and its certification is filed before filming begins. The endorsement for this is currently awaiting countersignature, so I want everyone aware of this constraint as we finalize the set design and construction plan.
transcript.speaker: A5
